description: We are aspiring developers passionate about software engineering, AI, data science, and NASA open data. We are building EMBERLENS, a platform to analyze NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire observations. We value collaboration, innovation, and practical solutions.
summary: EMBERLENS helps people explore where and when NASA satellites detected active-fire thermal anomalies across Bangladesh. It maps detections and compares monthly and historical patterns while keeping MODIS and VIIRS results separate, preserving each sensor’s confidence meaning and showing data provenance. The project uses a fixed historical snapshot; detections are not confirmed fires, and missing records do not prove there was no fire.
details:
EMBERLENS is an AI-powered fire intelligence platform designed to harmonize NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations and transform them into meaningful historical insights. It aims to create a consistent, sensor-aware record of fire activity, identify fire events, reconstruct long-term activity patterns, and analyze seasonality, historical baselines, unusual activity, and critical periods. Users will be able to explore fire activity through an interactive map and place-specific intelligence dashboard. EMBERLENS will also support researchers by providing downloadable observations, harmonized records, fire events, and analysis results with relevant metadata and data provenance. The goal is to move beyond displaying individual fire detections toward understanding how fire activity changes across locations and over time.

We are a team of aspiring developers passionate about software engineering, AI, data science, and building technology that solves real-world problems. Our interests include web development, data visualization, geospatial technologies, and using NASA's open data to create meaningful insights.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing EMBERLENS, a fire intelligence platform that aims to harmonize NASA MODIS and VIIRS observations, analyze historical fire activity, identify unusual patterns, and make the resulting data more accessible to researchers.

Our team is interested in building practical, data-driven solutions with a clean user experience and a strong technical foundation. We value collaboration, experimentation, knowledge sharing, and turning complex ideas into working prototypes.

We welcome participants with skills or interests in GIS and geospatial analysis, remote sensing, Python and machine learning, data science, frontend/backend development, UI/UX design, scientific research, and data visualization. Whether you are an experienced contributor or an enthusiastic learner, we would love to collaborate with people who are curious, proactive, and excited to build something meaningful with NASA data
